Sam Lott 2.2 The Justification for AMDs The premise of AMDs is that large-scale deployment of AV mobility services in the near to medium term will occur primarily in areas with sufficient development density to provide a viable population of potential users and destinations to serve. Although mobility providers within an AMD can aim for profitability from operations, as with other forms of transportation, these systems depend on public investment and infrastructural resources for operation. Environments for which AMD operations may be suited—such as dense urban settings, business and residential districts, and major activity centers like airports and university or medical campuses—exhibit dense and dispersed patterns of demand for relatively short person-trips. In many of these areas, mobility demand has been served primarily by private automobiles, which often fail to provide high-quality service because of slow speeds, congestion, and limited parking. These factors are notable for being part of the catalyst behind the interest and commercial success of ride-hailing companies over the past decade. Positioning the AMD’s AV circulation services as ubiquitous and readily accessible within an operating area can ensure the district can be most efficiently served by its automated mobility systems. Within the dense and dispersed origins and destinations of a geofenced AMD district, trips are relatively short—allowing fleets to meet demand using rightsized vehicles, typically lightweight small- to medium-sized vehicles. AMD management also aims to minimize “deadheading,” a term denoting the supporting portion of a trip during which no passenger is aboard a vehicle as it moves to serve a pickup request through applications of advanced vehicle assignment and routing algorithms. One advantage of AMDs in locations with development environments having 5 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies at www.nlr.gov/publications. dense populations and potential destinations is that mobility needs can be met without vehicle ownership and at greater convenience than the status quo. In addition, trip requests can be served by multiple AV fleets, operated by various entities, either public or private, and complemented by a rich mix of other manual modes including micromobility.
